plain.text: Jesus was back in Capernaum, and the house where he was staying was so packed that no one could get to the door. Four men carried a paralysed friend on a mat. They made a hole in the roof and lowered him down in front of Jesus. When Jesus saw their faith, he said, "Son, your sins are forgiven." Some religious teachers thought, "Only God can forgive sins!" Jesus knew what they were thinking. To show he had authority to forgive sins, he told the man, "Get up, take your mat and go home." The man got up and walked out in front of everyone. They were amazed and praised God.

Jesus saw Levi, a tax collector, sitting at his tax booth. "Follow me," he said, and Levi got up and followed him. Later, Jesus ate at Levi's house with many tax collectors and "sinners". Some Pharisees asked why he ate with such people. Jesus said, "Healthy people don't need a doctor, sick people do. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."

People asked why John's disciples and the Pharisees fasted but Jesus' disciples did not. Jesus said that guests at a wedding do not fast while the bridegroom is with them. A time would come when he would be taken away, and then they would fast. He added that you don't sew a new patch on old clothes or pour new wine into old wineskins. Something new had arrived.

One Sabbath, Jesus' disciples picked heads of grain as they walked through a field. The Pharisees complained that this was against the Sabbath rules. Jesus reminded them that King David once ate the special bread in God's house when he was hungry. Then he said, "The Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath. So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."

summary.bigIdea: Jesus has authority to forgive sins, and he welcomes people others reject.
points: Four friends bring a paralysed man to Jesus, who forgives and heals him.
Jesus calls a tax collector and eats with people others look down on.
Jesus says the Sabbath was made for people, and he is Lord of it.
summary.reflection: The paralysed man was carried by friends. Who could you help bring closer to Jesus, or who has done that for you?
